terms.grammar: also written as two words, aquae ductus

evidence: Cic. Att. 13.6.1: dē aquae ductū probē fēcistī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “a leading of water”; Frontinus wrote a book on Rome’s aqueducts, Dē aquae ductū urbis Rōmae.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 173, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 272.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
